newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: STORK TO BUY REST OF STORK KETELS.
newsitem.headline: STORK TO BUY REST OF STORK KETELS.

text.p: Industrial systems and services group Stork NV said on Friday it intends to buy the remaining 50 percent in Stork Ketels BV from Deutsche Babcock AG, making it a 100 percent Stork subsidiary.
Boilers to power plants maker Stork Ketels will be thoroughly reorganised, but this has been taken into account with previous forecasts, Stork said.
It added that it maintained its expectation that 1996 net profit will be higher than 1995's 108 million guilders.
The Dutch group said it expected the transfer of the remaining 50 percent stake in Stork Ketels to be finalised within the next few weeks. No financial details were given.
Stork said it will split up Stork Ketels' activities and merge them with other Stork subsidiaries after the reorganisation of the unit.

After the restructuring, the remaining activities are expected to generate a profitable turnover of 200 million guilders in 1997 and a total of about 460 employees will be involved. At the moment, Stork Ketels has about 730 employees.
Reorganisations which started earlier will reduce the number of jobs at Stork Ketels by 75 in 1996 and 1997. An additional restructuring will result in the loss of another 200 jobs.
This reorganisation has been taken into account with the valuation of the 50 percent stake in Stork Ketels from Deutsche Babcock, Stork said.

Deutsche Babcock previously announced it would spin off non-core business and said it expected a loss of 400 million marks in the 1995/96 financial year. In October it said restructuring costs would be higher than originally expected.
